qualifications: Lease-File.pdf (page 1) is image-only and returned no extractable text in this control, which has no image/OCR access. Consequently the authoritative unit 101 rent, expiry, security deposit, renewal-option terms and any lease amendments are UNKNOWN and were not guessed. This is the single largest unresolved evidence item, and Rent-Roll.xlsx note C15 explicitly flags it.

effective_monthly_base is therefore unresolved. The rent-roll-printed total of $60,700/month is reported for context only. Loan sizing is not affected: the underwriting plan supplies gross potential base rent of $900,000 (Property-and-Plan.pdf p.2) rather than deriving it from the rent roll.

Period labels are distinct and must not be conflated: T12 = September 2025 through August 2026 (actual, cash basis); rent roll = point-in-time as of 2026-08-31; underwriting plan = September 2026 forward (scenario). Annualized contractual rent ($60,700 x 12 = $728,400) does not equal T12 gross potential base rent ($852,000) and, per Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1, should not be forced to reconcile.

Historical vs. underwritten NOI/NCF are distinct: T12 NOI before reserves $592,800 and T12 NCF $575,800 versus underwritten NOI before reserves $760,710 and underwritten NCF $743,710. The uplift is driven by the supplied $900,000 GPR scenario and $195,000 other income, not by observed T12 collections.

Rates are distinct: contract rate 6.75% (index floored at 4.00% plus 2.75% spread) versus sizing rate 7.25% (underwriting floor). First-year contractual debt service is interest-only at 6.75% ($445,206), which is approximately $126,879 lower than the sizing debt service of $572,085. Illustratively, once amortization begins at the contractual 6.75% over 25 years, the annual payment would be roughly $547,000 on $6,595,638 - a material step-up from the IO year; this figure is derived, not stated in the packet.

DSCR is the binding constraint and sizes exactly to the 1.30x minimum, leaving no DSCR cushion. Debt yield at the maximum loan is 11.28% (versus a 10.00% minimum) and LTV headroom is roughly $166,000.
The 36-month maturity against a 25-year amortization schedule creates substantial balloon/refinance risk; only 24 months of amortization would occur before maturity given the 12-month IO period.

The insurer renewal confirmation itself (dated 2026-08-25, $33,600) is not included as a standalone document; the premium is asserted inside Property-and-Plan.pdf p.2. It is reported as the evidenced renewal premium per the packet's instruction, but a reviewer should require the actual binder/quote. It represents a 12% increase over the T12 actual of $30,000.

Lender-Terms.pdf is dated 2026-09-01 and is explicitly nonbinding indicative discussion terms; no credit approval, appraisal, environmental report, sponsor track record or market comparables were supplied. No market, sponsor or lender claims beyond the packet are made here, and no comps were researched or geocoded.
Valuation of $11,269,778 is a mechanical capitalization of underwritten NOI before reserves at the stated 6.75% cap rate; the term sheet states no appraisal is implied.

Tenant/lease concentration: unit 103 (Tenant C LLC, 30,000 SF, $27,000/month) is approximately 44.5% of contractual base rent, expiring 2029-08-31; unit 102 expires 2028-08-31, after the 36-month loan maturity horizon but relevant to takeout. Unit 104 (15,000 SF, 17.6% of area) is vacant with $12,500/month market rent that is not collected income. Physical occupancy is 75% by count and 82.35% by area, while the underwriting scenario applies only an 8% combined revenue loss to a $900,000 GPR - a reviewer should test whether that revenue-loss factor adequately reflects the vacant suite.

Sizing used unrounded intermediates per Lender-Terms.pdf; displayed currency is rounded for readability. The DSCR-constrained principal is stated as $6,595,638 and may vary by a few hundred dollars depending on the precision carried in the 0.0867368 annual constant. All dependent outputs (origination fee, IO debt service, cash to borrower, debt yield) scale accordingly.

T12 monthly columns were footed against the printed annual column for every line item (GPR, vacancy, concessions, bad debt, other income, each expense, and reserves) and all ties exactly, so no internal inconsistency was found in T12-Statement.pdf.

Per Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1, replacement reserves, capital improvements ($220,000 T12), loan principal and interest ($294,000 T12) and depreciation ($180,000 T12) are all below operating income and were excluded from operating expenses. Any reported 'property NOI' equal to cash flow after reserves is preserved conceptually but separated here into NOI before reserves and NCF after reserves.
This analysis is an internal-review underwriting work product only. It is not a legal opinion, appraisal, or credit commitment.
